title: Implement operator geo-guard and KMS accountability binding
author: Samir Patel
release_notes: Add operator-scoped geo-guard enforcing per-request claimed-region checks
Bind KMS key usage to operator service principal with region-awareness
Enrich audit events with immutable geo provenance headers
description:
Context and motivation: customers operating under jurisdictional constraints asked for stronger guarantees that operator-level actions cannot be used to exfiltrate or re-route tenant data across geozones. This PR implements a conservative, opt-in enforcement path that combines RBAC v2 operator-scoping, per-request claimed-region checks, and a KMS accountability binding so that KMS operations for tenant data must be attributed to a region-bound operator lease.

What this change does (summary):
- Adds an ingress 'operator geo-guard' middleware that validates claimed-region headers against operator leases and tenant residency assertions.
- Introduces a KMS accountability binding: a small runtime shim that rejects KMS Encrypt/Decrypt/Sign requests where the operator lease or service principal is not region-eligible for the tenant's pinned region.
- Extends the RBAC v2 policy model with an operator_scoped role template and a temporal-lease annotation for ephemeral operator grants.
- Enriches audit records with immutable provenance headers (X-RW-Region-Provenance, X-RW-Operator-Lease) and adds an audit-signer hook to prevent tampering between services.
- Adds a policy compiler check that rejects policy bundles which would accidentally grant cross-region KMS usage to an operator-scoped role.

Design notes and tradeoffs:
- Conservative enforcement: default is permissive for existing customers; enforcement can be toggled per-cluster/tenant via feature flags. This minimizes rollout blast radius while allowing early adopters to opt in.
- Compatibility: we only add new optional headers and policy templates; no changes to existing API surface. SDKs will be updated in a follow-up PR to surface operator-lease creation helpers.
- Security: the audit-signer uses existing KMS service keys (no new long-lived keys). We rely on existing trust in the control plane KMS; the shim binds service principal -> region at runtime.

Commit summary (high level):
- feat(ingress): add operator-geo-guard middleware with region claim validation
- feat(kms): introduce accountability binding and validation shim
- feat(rbac): add operator_scoped role template + temporal lease annotation
- feat(audit): emit X-RW-Region-Provenance and X-RW-Operator-Lease headers; signer hook
- test: unit + integration tests for middleware and KMS shim
- docs: runbook and operator-facing migration notes

Changed areas (high level):
- services/ingress/middleware/geo_guard.go -- new middleware and unit tests
- services/kms/accountability/shim.go -- binding logic and validation rules
- pkg/rbac/templates/operator_scoped.yaml -- new role template and examples
- tools/policy-compiler/checks/region_bindings.go -- compile-time safety check
- services/audit/signer/signer.go -- add provenance enrichment and verification
- docs/security/operator-geo-guard.md -- design and rollout guide

Small illustrative snippet (middleware validation):
- The guard checks X-RW-Claimed-Region against tenant.metadata.residency_pin and operatorLease.Region. If mismatch and enforcement enabled -> 403 + audit entry.

Migration plan:
1) Deploy in permissive mode (log-only) for 2 weeks, surface audit events to SRE and Compliance dashboards.
2) Reach out to top-10 tenants with cross-region traffic to validate false-positive rate.
3) Flip enforcement for customers who opted in.
4) Rollout to default-on in a future release after 4-week telemetry window.

Testing and QA:
- Unit tests for middleware (region mismatch, missing headers, lease expiration) added.
- Integration tests deploy a lightweight KMS stub to simulate cross-region requests and validate shim rejection paths.
- Added a chaos test that simulates operator lease rotation while requests are in-flight to validate graceful failures.

Related work and references:
- ENG-4219 (Linear): operator geo-guard epic
- SEC-78: compliance checklist for residency proofs
- Previously discussed at design review (link internal): https://linear.app/redwood/issue/ENG-4219/operator-geo-guard

Rollback plan:
- Feature flagging present on both middleware and KMS shim; full rollback is flipping flags followed by a small config change to revert policy compiler if necessary.

Author notes:
- I intentionally kept audit header names stable and namespaced (X-RW-*) to make later filtering straightforward.
- This PR focuses on enforceable operator scoping; a follow-up will add tenant-level signed residency proofs to further reduce reliance on operator assertions.
